notes: Lumber names use store sizes such as 1×6 and 2×4. Listed cut lengths and sheet cuts are exact finished dimensions. The 3D model retains actual geometry; this labeling change does not change what to buy or how long to cut it.
Prices observed with E Bradenton selected; availability can change. Tax, delivery, tools, paint, primer, floor materials and panel-to-panel/corner connections excluded.
Whole retail packs are rounded after combining requirements. Adhesive allowance is one 16 oz bottle per four panels, rounded up; actual use depends on application.
The 10×4 panel quantities match the current website model. This is a construction prototype, not structural validation.
10-foot facing uses a 48×96 lower sheet and 48×24 upper strip. Allowing saw kerf, only three full 24-inch strips fit a second 96-inch sheet.

8-foot ballast is the existing provisional 75 lb assumption. Fill four bags to about 19 lb each and stand them in a row along the shelf between both crossbars; supplied sandbag shape differs from the schematic.
10-foot required ballast mass, bag count and retention layout are unresolved; no complete freestanding total is presented.
Choose straight, sound dry lumber and measure supplied stock. Pilot drill and verify proposed screw sizes in the prototype. Use matched-thickness pads at all bearing points.

Screw-only jack revision, Oct 7, 2026: six #8 × 1¼ in wood screws per jack, driven from the stile into the upright, heads flush. Two actual ¾ in boards provide ½ in nominal penetration into the upright. Prototype connection: verify on scrap, avoid splits/over-countersinking, and replace wood with stripped holes. Keep the flat supported during assembly and removal. Staples fasten the skin; do not substitute them or nails at the jack attachment.

Only the #8 × 1¼ in screw pack was rechecked Oct 7, 2026: Home Depot #6319, model 801832, SKU 251429, internet 204275496, $7.97 per 100-pack, 6 packs shown in stock. Other product check dates remain as listed.

Both options add a separate 48 person-hour compound-corner planning allowance plus 3–5 drying calendar days; this is not a published construction-time benchmark.
